test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 28 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A trader offers one kitchen set free with each kitchen set purchased at the marked price. If he still makes a profit of 20%, at what percentage above the cost price has the trader marked the kitchen set?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Buy 1 get 1 free means 1 item is free out of 2 total items.

Discount % = (Free items ÷ Total items) × 100 = (1 ÷ 2) × 100 = 50%.

Using the direct ratio formula: CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%)

CP / MP = (100 − 50) / (100 + 20) = 50 / 120 = 5 / 12

Markup % = [(MP − CP) / CP] × 100 = [(12 − 5) / 5] × 100 = (7 / 5) × 100 = 140%.

**∴ The correct answer is 140%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Offer: Buy 1 kitchen set, get 1 free.

Profit earned = 20%.

 
 Buy 1 (Paid)
 Customer pays
 1 MP

 
 Get 1 (Free)
 Customer gets
 without cost

 Total items given = 2
 Effective Selling Price (SP) = 1 MP

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of 1 kitchen set be 100.

⇒ The trader gives 2 kitchen sets in total (1 paid + 1 free).

⇒ Total Cost Price for the trader = 2 × 100 = 200.

⇒ The trader earns a 20% profit on his total cost.

⇒ Total Selling Price (SP) = Total CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

⇒ Total SP = 200 × (100 + 20) ÷ 100 = 200 × 1.20 = 240.

⇒ The customer only pays for 1 item at its Marked Price (MP).

⇒ Therefore, MP of 1 kitchen set = Total SP = 240.

⇒ CP of 1 kitchen set is 100.

⇒ Markup % = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

⇒ Markup % = [(240 − 100) ÷ 100] × 100 = (140 ÷ 100) × 100 = 140%.

**∴ The correct answer is 140%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Buy X Get Y Free Discount

The effective discount percentage is calculated on the total number of items provided to the customer: D% = [Y ÷ (X + Y)] × 100.

CP and MP Relationship

When both profit percentage and discount percentage are known, the direct ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price is: CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%).

Markup Percentage

The percentage by which the Marked Price is raised above the original Cost Price: Markup % = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.
